input_oneliner: Rapid page: 68F HTN, AF on apixaban, RN found L facial droop and slurred speech, last seen normal 40 min ago

reference_targets_freetext.item: Forehead sparing (facial symmetry: raise eyebrows, close eyes tightly; compare upper versus lower face weakness)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Forehead sparing indicates an upper motor neuron (central) lesion; forehead involvement points to a peripheral facial nerve palsy

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pronator drift and side-to-side arm and leg strength
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Arm drift is a Cincinnati stroke item; with facial paresis or abnormal speech it establishes a central lesion (Goldstein 2005 RCE)

reference_targets_freetext.item: Speech and language testing: dysarthria versus aphasia (read a sentence, name objects, repeat)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Abnormal speech is a Cincinnati item; aphasia is cortical, dysarthria alone is compatible with either lesion
Gaze preference localizes a hemispheric lesion and is incompatible with Bell palsy
A field cut indicates a cortical lesion
Time window determines eligibility for reperfusion therapy

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about apixaban adherence and time of last dose
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Anticoagulant status determines thrombolysis eligibility and hemorrhage risk

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about headache, neck pain, and vomiting
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Severe headache or vomiting with a focal deficit raises concern for hemorrhage

off_bedside_acceptable: Non-contrast CT head and CT angiography
should_not_recommend: Delaying stroke alert to complete a full neurologic examination
Prednisone for presumed Bell palsy without testing forehead sparing and limb strength
Antiplatelet or anticoagulant before imaging excludes hemorrhage

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: added: droop involves the forehead and the eye will not close
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: Rapid page: 68F HTN, AF on apixaban, RN found L facial droop involving forehead and cannot close L eye, slurred speech, last seen normal 40 min ago
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Bell palsy rises to co-leading differential; forehead sparing check remains must-have; pronator drift, gaze deviation, visual fields, and speech/language testing remain but become confirmatory rather than the lead; otoscopy for ear canal vesicles and questions about ear pain, hyperacusis, and taste change rise.
